class.name: VoxelEngine
class.brief_description: High-level facade for managing voxel terrain generation and configuration.
class.description:
[b]VoxelEngine[/b] is a simplified entry point for using the terrain generation system. It manages the lifecycle of a [VoxelGenerator] instance and provides convenient factory methods for creating terrain.
[b]Key Features:[/b] [ul] [li]Single-point access to voxel terrain generation[/li] [li]Automatic lifecycle management of VoxelGenerator[/li] [li]Terrain loading from configuration files (.tres)[/li] [li]Simple voxel read/write API[/li] [/ul]
[b]Architecture:[/b] VoxelEngine acts as a [Node] manager that owns a [VoxelGenerator] instance. When a VoxelEngine node is freed from the scene tree, it automatically cleans up its owned VoxelGenerator. This pattern is recommended for most gameplay scenarios where you want simple, integrated terrain management.
[b]Usage Pattern:[/b] [code] extends Node
func _ready(): var engine = VoxelEngine.new() add_child(engine) var generator = engine.create_generator() # Configure generator as needed generator.set_world_size(Vector3i(16, 16, 16)) generator.generate() [/code]
[b]Alternative: Direct VoxelGenerator[/b] For advanced use cases, you can instantiate [VoxelGenerator] directly without VoxelEngine for more control over lifecycle.
[b]Related Classes:[/b] [ul] [li][VoxelGenerator] - Core terrain generation engine[/li] [li][TerrainConfig] - Reusable terrain configuration resource[/li] [/ul]

method.name: create_generator
method.description:
Creates a new [VoxelGenerator] instance and stores it as owned by this VoxelEngine. The VoxelEngine maintains ownership of the generator and will automatically delete it when the VoxelEngine node is freed.
If a generator already exists, it is destroyed before creating the new one.
[b]Return Value:[/b] A newly created [VoxelGenerator] instance ready for configuration.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var engine = VoxelEngine.new() var gen = engine.create_generator() gen.set_resolution(2) gen.generate() [/code]

method.name: destroy_generator
method.description:
Explicitly destroys the owned [VoxelGenerator]. Calling this is optional - the generator is automatically destroyed when the VoxelEngine is freed.
This is useful when you want to reset the generator without destroying the VoxelEngine node itself.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread. If generation is in progress, ensure it's cancelled first.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] engine.destroy_generator() # Generator is now null, safe to create a new one var new_gen = engine.create_generator() [/code]

method.name: get_voxel_generator
method.description:
Returns the currently owned [VoxelGenerator] instance, or [code]null[/code] if no generator exists.
[b]Return Value:[/b] The [VoxelGenerator] instance, or null.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread, but the returned generator should only be configured/used from the main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var gen = engine.get_voxel_generator() if gen != null: gen.set_debug_mode(true) [/code]

method.name: load_terrain
method.description:
Loads a terrain configuration from a resource file and creates/configures a [VoxelGenerator] with those settings.
This method: [ol] [li]Loads the configuration from [code]res://configs/{terrain_name}.tres[/code][/li] [li]Creates a new [VoxelGenerator] (destroying any existing one)[/li] [li]Applies the configuration to the generator[/li] [li]Returns the configured generator[/li] [/ol]
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]terrain_name[/code] - Name of the terrain configuration (without path or extension). For example, "grassland" loads "res://configs/grassland.tres".
[b]Return Value:[/b] The newly created and configured [VoxelGenerator], or null if the configuration file cannot be loaded.
[b]File Format:[/b] The configuration file must be a [TerrainConfig] resource (.tres format).
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var gen = engine.load_terrain("grassland") if gen != null: gen.generate_async() [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method TerrainConfig.apply_to_voxel_generator]

method.name: set_voxel_generator_node
method.description:
[b]DEPRECATED:[/b] This method is kept for backward compatibility. Use [method create_generator] instead.
Previously this method allowed setting a pre-existing [VoxelGenerator] node as the managed generator. This functionality is discouraged in favor of the factory pattern.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread.

method.name: set_voxel
method.description:
Sets a voxel at the given world position to the specified voxel type.
This is a convenience method that proxies the call to the owned [VoxelGenerator].
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]position[/code] - World position of the voxel (in voxel coordinates). [code]type[/code] - The voxel type ID to set. Voxel type IDs are defined by your voxel registry.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Must be called from the main thread.
[b]Performance Note:[/b] Setting individual voxels is relatively slow. For bulk terrain modifications, use [method VoxelGenerator.modify_terrain] instead with terrain edits.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] engine.set_voxel(Vector3i(100, 50, 100), 1) # Set stone at position [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method get_voxel], [method VoxelGenerator.set_voxel], [method VoxelGenerator.modify_terrain]

method.name: get_voxel
method.description:
Gets the voxel type at the given world position.
This is a convenience method that proxies the call to the owned [VoxelGenerator].
[b]Parameters:[/b] [code]position[/code] - World position of the voxel (in voxel coordinates).
[b]Return Value:[/b] The voxel type ID at the position, or 0 if the voxel doesn't exist or is air.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var voxel_type = engine.get_voxel(Vector3i(100, 50, 100)) print("Voxel type: ", voxel_type) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method set_voxel], [method VoxelGenerator.get_voxel_at]

method.name: get_total_voxel_count
method.description:
Returns the total number of voxels in the currently loaded world.
This is calculated as: [code]world_size.x * world_size.y * world_size.z * (chunk_size ^ 3)[/code]
[b]Return Value:[/b] The total number of voxels in the world as a 64-bit integer.
[b]Performance Note:[/b] This is a cheap O(1) calculation.
[b]Thread Safety:[/b] Safe to call from any thread.
[b]Example:[/b] [code] var total = engine.get_total_voxel_count() print("Total voxels: ", total) [/code]
[b]See Also:[/b] [method VoxelGenerator.set_world_size], [method VoxelGenerator.set_chunk_size]
